319441.title: The major-arcs conjecture for exceptional sets of additive problems

literal_gate.statement:
Let ${\mathcal A},{\mathcal B}\subseteq {\mathbb N}$. Write $\overline{{\mathcal A}+{\mathcal B}}$ for the exceptional set associated with the sumset ${\mathcal A}+{\mathcal B}$, let $|\mathcal B|_0^N$ denote the number of elements of ${\mathcal B}$ up to $N$, and let $\widehat {\Upsilon}(\overline{{\mathcal A}+{\mathcal B}},{\mathcal B};N)$ be the corresponding exceptional-set counting function. **Major-arcs conjecture.** One has

$$
\widehat {\Upsilon}(\overline{{\mathcal A}+{\mathcal B}},{\mathcal B};N)\ll N^{\varepsilon-1}\left(\left|\overline{{\mathcal A}+{\mathcal B}}\right|_{2N}^{3N}|{\mathcal B}|_0^N\right)^2.
$$

This estimate is suggested by a heuristic application of the Hardy–Littlewood method and would quantify the expected improvement in exceptional-set estimates obtained by adding ${\mathcal B}$. The source presents it as a speculation rather than a proved result.

319494.title: Droms–Mellinger–Meyer dimension conjecture for projective-plane LDPC codes

literal_gate.statement:
Let $q$ be an odd prime power, and let ${\mathbf B}$ and ${\mathbf B}_0$ be the incidence matrices of internal points versus secant lines and external points versus passant lines, respectively, in ${\mathrm{PG}}(2,q)$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{L}_0$ be their column $\mathbb F_2$-null spaces. **Droms–Mellinger–Meyer's conjecture.** The dimensions are

$$
\dim_{\mathbb F_2}(\mathcal{L})=\begin{cases}\frac{q^2-1}{4}-q,&q\equiv1\pmod4,\\frac{q^2-1}{4}-q+1,&q\equiv3\pmod4,
\end{cases}
$$

and

$$
\dim_{\mathbb F_2}(\mathcal{L}_0)=\begin{cases}\frac{q^2-1}{4},&q\equiv1\pmod4,\\frac{q^2-1}{4}+1,&q\equiv3\pmod4.
\end{cases}
$$

These formulas concern the dimensions of the four low-density parity-check codes constructed from submatrices of the point-line incidence matrix of ${\mathrm{PG}}(2,q)$. The article confirms this conjecture, so the claim is solved.

320040.title: White's conjecture for lattice path polymatroids

literal_gate.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a lattice path polymatroid. Its base ring is the polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[Y_m: m$ is a basis of $\Gamma]$, and its toric ideal is the kernel of the map

$$
\phi: \mathbb{C}[Y_m: m \text{ is a basis of }\Gamma] \longrightarrow \mathbb{C}[x_0,x_1,x_2,\ldots],
$$

defined by $\phi(Y_{m_1}Y_{m_2}\cdots Y_{m_t})=m_1m_2\cdots m_t$. A **symmetric exchange binomial** is a binomial $Y_mY_{m'}-Y_nY_{n'}$ obtained when $n$ and $n'$ are obtained from $m$ and $m'$ by a symmetric exchange. **White's conjecture, adapted for polymatroids.** The toric ideal of $\Gamma$ is generated by symmetric exchange binomials. The paper proves this statement for lattice path polymatroids, so it is solved in the stated class, although the broader polymatroid version is presented as an adaptation of White's conjecture.

320198.title: Symmetry and central-circuit conjectures for ({1,2,3},6)- and ({2,3},6)-spheres

literal_gate.statement:
A $(\{1,2,3\},6)$-sphere is a sphere whose face sizes belong to $\{1,2,3\}$ and whose vertex degree is $6$; a $(\{2,3\},6)$-sphere is defined similarly with face sizes in $\{2,3\}$. A sphere is **$z$-knotted** or **$c$-knotted** when it has only one zigzag or only one central circuit, respectively. Its symmetry is denoted by the corresponding point-group symbol, and its $c$- and $z$-vectors record the lengths of its central circuits and zigzags.

**Symmetry and circuit conjecture.** (i) A $z$- or $c$-knotted $(\{1,2,3\},6)$-sphere, except Trifolium $C_{3v}$, has symmetry $C_1$, $C_2$, $C_3$, $D_2$ or $D_3$. (ii) A $(\{2,3\},6)$-sphere with only simple central circuits has symmetry $T_d$, $T_h$, $D_{6h}$, $D_{3d}$, $D_{2d}$, $D_{2h}$, $D_3$, $C_{2h}$ or $C_{3v}$. (iii) A $(\{1,2,3\},6)$-sphere of symmetry $D_{6h}$, $T_h$ or $T_d$ has only simple central circuits and zigzags. (iv) A $(\{2,3\},6)$-sphere of symmetry $T_d$ has $v=4x^2$ vertices, $c$-vector $(3x)^{4x}$ and $z$-vector $(6x)^{4x}$. (v) A $(\{2,3\},6)$-sphere of symmetry $T_h$ has $12x^2$ vertices, $c$-vector $(6x)^{6x}$ and $z$-vector $(12x)^{6x}$.

These assertions classify the possible symmetries and circuit structures in several highly symmetric or knotted families of discrete spheres. The supplied text gives no evidence that the conjecture has been proved or refuted.

320265.title: Ross's sub-lattice conjecture for periodic framework rigidity

literal_gate.statement: Let $\tilde{G}(\mathbf{p},\mathbf{L})$ be an infinitesimally rigid periodic framework with periodic graph $(\tilde{G},\varphi)$. Let $\Lambda<\mathbb{Z}^2$ be any sub-lattice, and define $(\tilde{G},\varphi')$ to be the periodic graph obtained by replacing the $\mathbb{Z}^2$-action $\varphi$ with the induced $\Lambda$-action $\varphi'$. **Ross's conjecture.** Then $\tilde{G}(\mathbf{p},\mathbf{L})$ is an infinitesimally rigid realization of the induced abstract periodic framework on $(\tilde{G},\varphi')$. Informally, this says that a generic rigid periodic framework remains rigid when the periodicity constraint is relaxed to a sub-lattice, enlarging the class of allowed motions. The conjecture concerns whether infinitesimal rigidity is preserved under passage from the original lattice to any sub-lattice; its resolution is not given here.

321624.title: Semi-Kotzig-frame double cover conjecture

literal_gate.statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph. A **frame** of $G$ is a spanning subgraph $H$ such that the contraction $G/H$ is even. For a subgraph $H$, let $\overline{H}$ denote the graph obtained by suppressing all degree-$2$ vertices. A **semi-Kotzig frame** is a frame whose every non-circuit component has suppressed graph a semi-Kotzig graph. A **$6$-even-subgraph double cover** is a double cover consisting of six even subgraphs.

**Semi-Kotzig-frame conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph with a semi-Kotzig frame has a $6$-even-subgraph double cover.

This strengthens the preceding Kotzig-frame conjecture by replacing Kotzig frames with the more general semi-Kotzig frames. The paper proves the result for semi-Kotzig frames with at most one non-circuit component, while the unrestricted statement remains open.

322777.title: The equal-block minimizer conjecture for multipartite flag-complex constructions

literal_gate.statement:
Let $1\leq p<k<r$ be integers, and let $m,n$ be real numbers satisfying

$$
m>{r\choose k}n^{k/r}.
$$

Define $w(i)=k$ if $i\leq k$ and $w(i)=r$ if $i>k$. Consider positive real numbers $a_1^k,\dots,a_k^k,a_1^r,\dots,a_r^r$ satisfying

$$
n=a_1^r a_2^r\dots a_r^r,
$$

$$
m=\sum_{i_1<i_2<\dots<i_k}a_{i_1}^{w(i_k)}a_{i_2}^{w(i_k)}\dots a_{i_k}^{w(i_k)},
$$

with $a_i^k\geq a_j^k$ whenever $i<j$ and $a_j^i\geq a_j^k$ whenever $i<k$.

**Equal-block minimizer conjecture.** The unique choice of constants minimizing

$$
\sum_{i_1<i_2<\dots<i_p}a_{i_1}^{w(i_p)}a_{i_2}^{w(i_p)}\dots a_{i_p}^{w(i_p)}
$$

is also the unique choice satisfying

$$
a_1^k=\dots=a_k^k=a_1^r=\dots=a_k^r>a_{k+1}^r=\dots=a_r^r.
$$

This conjecture identifies the proposed extremal pattern for minimizing lower-dimensional faces after fixing the numbers of $k$- and $r$-faces. It is presented as an explanation for why equal parameters within the relevant blocks are a natural construction, but its general validity remains open.

377044.title: The points-and-lines conjecture for free and K(pi,1) arrangements

literal_gate.statement:
Let ${\mathcal A}$ be a hyperplane arrangement with underlying matroid $G$. The **points** of $G$ are its flats of rank one, and its **lines** are its flats of rank two. Saying that $G$ is determined by its points and lines means that the matroid structure is uniquely determined by these rank-one and rank-two flats.

**Points-and-lines conjecture.** The underlying matroid of a free or $K(\pi,1)$ arrangement is determined by its points and lines.

This conjecture would imply that the combinatorial structure of matroids underlying free or $K(\pi,1)$ arrangements is controlled by rank-one and rank-two data. The text connects it to Terao’s freeness conjecture and the matroidality of the homotopy type of arrangement complements, but supplies no resolution.
